newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end lower, off lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end lower, off lows.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed lower but well off the lowest levels of the day after a choppy session.

Traders again focused on the interest rate market, where firm prices boosted index contracts early, only to come under pressure later in the day, which prompted selling in index futures, traders said.
The volatile price movement pushed the June S&P 500 contract far enough away from its theoretical fair value premium to trigger both arbitrage buy and sell programs, traders said.

Early buy programs were activated when the premium of June over the spot S&P index widened above about 8.25 points, while sell programs were hit when the premium narrowed below about 6.65 points, traders said.

Adding to volatility was the upcoming expiration, which resulted in various positioning by players, including rolling of March positions into June and shifting of arbitrage positions forward to the next month.
Traders noted, however, that open interest remained somewhat high given that there is only one more session before the expiration at the close of business Thursday.

Jay Hohmann, head futures trader at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities, noted that today's decline pushed the cash S&P 500 index below the lower trendline of an upward sloping channel, which came in at about 786.64 today.
The trendline dated back to July of last year, and the break could mean a fall to 750.00 "might be possible eventually. That would be a buying opportunity," Hohmann said.
Another day of steep declines in the Nasdaq 100 index also added to negative sentiment.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures closed slightly higher, closely following movement in U.S. contracts and finishing on a firm note.

At settlement, June S&P 500s were off 2.75 points at 792.25, Nasdaq 100s were 14.00 lower at 823.50, Russell 2000s were down 3.70 points at 353.30, KCBT Value Line futures were down 4.50 points at 707.50, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 50.0 to 18,525.0 and Midcap 400s fell 3.25 points to 260.55.
